name: retrain-tools
description: Submit training and evaluation jobs, inspect results, and select the policy to score.
---

# Environment tools

Read `ENVIRONMENT.json` for the site's policy, adapter composition and enforced constraints, and `tasks.json`
for task details. `STATUS.json` contains the latest budget, loaded stack, adapters and running job IDs.
`SCOREBOARD.md` has dev scores and lineage. While a train or eval is submitted, `jobs/<id>.json` (`progress`, `progress_line`; `status.py`),
STATUS.json (`job_progress`) and the scoreboard show whether it is queued (not started, with its queue time so far) or running, and for a
running train its completed steps, latest mean reward and GPU-hours so far, as the site reports them. `tasks/<task>/eval_prompt.txt` (when
the site provides it) is the prompt the policy receives at evaluation; training prompts are checked against it. `tasks/INDEX.md` lists each task's goal line, dev and
hidden seed ranges, recorded base score, API names and key rules, taken from tasks.json, the eval prompts and the base scores. State comes from the environment; this skill is editable guidance.

| Command | Effect |
| --- | --- |
| `python3 train.py SPEC` | Submit JSON/YAML spec to the installed trainer; see `skills/trainer/SKILL.md`. |
| `python3 eval.py --adapter A[,B...]\|base\|loaded --task T --seeds N` | Evaluate on the next N unused dev seeds (the result lists them; the base column has its own) with the task's `tasks/<task>/eval_prompt.txt` verbatim (no training `note`/`goal`; the final score uses the same prompt). A stack's score on a task is known only from an eval of that stack (`--adapter A,B`); neither the scoreboard nor the environment derives it from its adapters' single scores. `loaded` is the stack loaded when the request is picked up, so not an adapter whose train is still running. Results are written only when all seeds finish, so an eval that reaches its time limit usually fails with no count (rarely: a count over the seeds that finished, with `partial`). Where the site can resume an eval (eval port dq-t1v2), an eval stopped by the cluster (time limit, preemption, node failure) continues its remaining seeds in a new Slurm job, at most 3 times; its status then says `continued from seed k in job J`, and its result lists every Slurm job (`jobs`) and each continuation (`continued`: `job` stopped, `cause`, `from` seed, `of` seeds, `continued_in` job), as it lists site retries. |
| `python3 load.py load A [B...]` | Replace the loaded stack (names separated by spaces; eval.py separates them by commas). |
| `python3 load.py stack A [B...]` | Append to the loaded stack. |
| `python3 load.py unload [A...]` | Remove names, or return to base with no names. |
| `python3 status.py [ID...]` | Read job states and results; no IDs shows all jobs. The last line states what finishing now would score. |
| `python3 wait.py all\|ID... [--max 4h\|90m]` | Submit a wait barrier: your next turn starts when those jobs finish or after `--max` (default 2h), whichever comes first. If the bound comes first, the result states each job's queue state, reason, position and time pending, and "no job finished". The barrier runs in the environment after your command returns, so `--max` is not limited by the per-command time limit. |
| `python3 finish.py [--policy base \| --adapters A[,B...]] [--note TEXT]` | Step one of ending the session: submit the policy to score (no policy arguments: the loaded stack; single mode: `current`, `v<k>` or `current@<k>`). The result states exactly what will be scored and a token. |
| `python3 finish.py --confirm TOKEN` | Step two, in a later turn: end the session; the submission is scored. |
| `python3 cancel.py ID` | Stop a running train or eval. A train keeps the adapter of its last saved step (if the site saved one), registered with the steps it ran; the job is charged the GPU time it used. |

Scripts submit request files and return IDs. Shell success means submission, not job success. In the chat backend,
requests are handled only after the entire command returns: `train.py spec.json; wait.py all; load.py load a1`
queues a dependency chain, but reading status later in that same shell still sees the old state. The Codex backend has a background executor; request processing and status refresh happen independently.
Read `jobs/<id>.json` or the next observation to distinguish done, failed and refused requests.

Training names are reserved while pending. Training does not load an adapter in library mode; single mode automatically
replaces and loads `current`. When ENVIRONMENT.json `constraint` names versions, every successful train is a new version
v1, v2, ... (`current` = the latest) and becomes active; `load.py load v<k>` makes an earlier version active again,
`eval.py --adapter v<k>` evaluates one, the next train starts from the active version, and versions are never stacked.
Adapter composition depends on the site. Load calls are free. Train/dev calls reserve the
site's cost estimate at admission and are charged the site's cost per call (skills/trainer/SKILL.md, Cost); the
reservation is admission control, not a hard runtime cutoff.

Successful training returns an adapter path, a skills digest, and site-provided training metadata when available.
`training.json` in the adapter contains site-resolved parameters and artifact names. `site_sources` identifies the site
code, not the complete external GPU/software environment. A skill edit alone does not change the installed trainer.

Ending the session takes two steps: `finish.py` submits a policy and its result states exactly what will be scored
(adapters with version and weights sha, eval-prompt hash) and a token; `finish.py --confirm TOKEN` in a later turn ends the
session. Until then the session goes on; a `load.py` or `train.py` request in between cancels the submission (submit
again). An unknown adapter name refuses the submission. The submission is scored even if a different stack is loaded at
the end. If the session ends without a confirmation (budget, caps), the pending submission is scored, else the loaded
stack. Submitted jobs finish before the score. A file named `DONE` starts the two-step finish like `finish.py` with no
arguments: it submits the loaded stack (the file is removed); the session ends only after `finish.py --confirm TOKEN`.

Relative paths in SPEC (a reward file, an init adapter path, data files) resolve against the workspace, where `train.py` runs, wherever SPEC itself is. The programs can call exactly the functions listed under `APIs:` in the task's eval_prompt.txt. The Key rules of the stack, revstack, stackv2 and handover prompts also name `get_object_pose`, `sample_grasp_pose`, `goto_pose_arm*` and a `z_approach` parameter: none of these exists in these cells (the rules text is shared with the tasks' privileged-API variant). The prompts are the benchmark's cells of record and are scored as they are. A stack (`eval.py --adapter A,B`, `load.py stack`) holds at most 2 adapters: each is rank 32 and the serving's maximum LoRA rank is 64; a larger stack ends `failed` with `stack rank 96 > 64 (the serving's --max-lora-rank): at most 2 adapters of rank 32`. Your shell on this site writes only in the workspace and has no network (pip, curl and similar fail) and no Slurm client; all compute goes through train.py and eval.py. ## What a practice call is GRPO on LoRA adapters of the policy model named in SCOREBOARD.md's `policy:` line (LoRA rank 32, alpha 64, on q,k,v,o,out,gate,up,down projections for Qwen3.8-27B; other policies have no `out`). Each step: `batch` prompts x 8 rollouts. GRPO's update comes from reward differences among a prompt's 8 rollouts: a prompt whose rollouts all get the same reward adds nothing to it. A rollout is one program written by the model for the task, run once in the task's simulator on one seed; its score is the reward below. The training prompt is the task's evaluation prompt, byte for byte (checked before training), unless the spec sets `note` or `goal` or a `data` row sets `prompt`: those are part of the training prompt only. Every eval, including the final hidden-seed score, uses the task's `tasks//eval_prompt.txt` in the workspace verbatim, without any note or goal. Sampling during practice: temperature 1.0, top_p 0.95, top_k 20; at most 8192 generated tokens per program. Sampling during evaluation (eval.py and the final score): temperature 0.7, top_p 0.8, top_k 20, presence_penalty 1.5, thinking off; at most 8192 generated tokens per program (envs/capx/config_of_record_v4.yaml). For lift, stack, wipe and nut the practice unit and the eval cell run the same task config (`*_reduced_api_exampleless.yaml` is the s4:paper cell's config). A policy whose name carries `+init:` (SCOREBOARD.md's `policy:` line) is the model plus that init adapter: its base is served with the init, every train without `init` starts from it, so each trained adapter already contains the init's change, and a stack of two such adapters applies that change twice. ## Spec fields (a spec with any other field fails; see Failures) | field | type | default | accepted | |---|---|---|---| | `task` | string or list | required unless `data` | a trainable task (see workspace/tasks/INDEX.md), or a list of them: one call practising all, every batch split equally across them (`batch` a multiple of their number; no `note` / `goal`); revstack practises alone | | `name` | string | `a` | letters, digits, `_ . -`, at most 48; not already taken, not `base` / `loaded`. Single-adapter mode: omit it (or `current`) | | `steps` | integer | 1 | any positive integer (cost grows with it, see below) | | `batch` | integer | 8 | prompts per step (each x 8 rollouts) | | `lr` | float | 2e-5 | learning rate | | `init` | string | none (fresh LoRA) | an adapter name produced by an earlier train of this session (`base` is not one: omit `init` to start from the policy). Single-adapter mode: omit it (or `current`); every train continues `current`. The new adapter is the init adapter continued (it already holds init's change): loading both stacks that change twice | | `start_preset` | string | none | a named start-state preset (core/start_presets.py: `restack_grasped`/`restack_lifted`/`restack_aligned`, `nut_grasped`/`nut_aligned`) to begin practice from an intermediate scene (e.g. object already grasped) so the agent trains the hard tail; the staged reward then scores only the stages after that sub-goal; fails loudly if the preset has not been built. With hidden tasks (B2): also the name of a preset you built with `preset.py` (`presets/.json`), on the task it was built on; on a hidden task only such a preset | | `start_mix` | string | none | a mixed start-state pool (core/mix_presets.py, built with `build_mix`): seeds split across presets of one task at a ratio, some from scratch; the staged reward scores the full chain; not with `start_preset`; fails loudly if not built; refused on a hidden task (B2) | | `reward` | string | `task_completed` | `task_completed` (1.0 if the task's own success check passes, else 0.0); `shaped` (the simulator's staged reward); Python source containing `def reward(r)`; or the path of a `.py` file (relative paths: the workspace) defining `reward(r)`. `r` is the simulator's reply: `task_completed`, `reward`, `sandbox_rc`, `seed`, `log_tail` (keys or attributes); return a float | | `seed_start` | integer | 810001 | rollout k of the call runs on seed `seed_start + k`; must not reach seeds 1-100 | | `note` | string | none | one sentence inserted after the training prompt's Goal line (not a comment: the rollouts see it; evaluation prompts never have it) | | `goal` | string | none | replaces the training prompt's Goal line (evaluation prompts keep theirs) | | `time` | string | set by the site: 1 GPU 25 min + 13 min x steps, 2 GPUs 85 min + 17 min x steps, 3 GPUs 30 min + 14 min x steps, at least 2 h (whole minutes, rounded up; the job record's `config` shows the value used) | wall limit of each Slurm job of the call, `HH:MM:SS`; a call whose job reaches it continues from its last saved step (below); once it has continued 3 times it keeps the adapter of its last saved step, as a cancel (result `time_limit`; a preempted or node-failed call likewise, result `preempted` / `node_fail`), or ends `failed` with the fact if none was saved | | `data` | string | none | a JSONL file of training prompts in your workspace: see Training data below. With `data`, the tasks, seeds, order and steps come from its rows | | `objective` | string | `grpo` | `grpo` (the practice call above) or `sft` (supervised fine-tuning on your own demonstrations: see SFT below; its spec has `data` and the fields of that section only) | | `epochs` | integer | 1 | `objective: sft` only: passes over the kept rows | | `min_reward` | number | 1.0 | `objective: sft` only: rows with `reward` >= this are trained on, the others dropped (a filter, never a weight) | ## Training data (`data`) `data` names a JSONL file in your workspace (a path relative to the workspace, or absolute inside it): one line per training prompt, `{"task": ..., "seed": ..., "variant": ..., "prompt": ...}` (`variant` and `prompt` optional, no other keys): - `task`: a trainable task. `variant`: another trainable task of the same simulator task (e.g. `stack` with variant `revstack`; revstack runs under a scene shift and practises alone, so a dataset with revstack rows has no rows of any other task); the row then trains on `variant`. Any mixture of tasks and variants is allowed. - `seed`: an integer >= 810001 (seeds 1-100 are the final score's, 800001-809999 are eval.py's dev seeds); all 8 rollouts of the row run on that seed. - `prompt`: replaces the task's user message for that row only (the system message stays).
